brand_names: Advil PM (note: some versions use ibuprofen)
drug_class: Analgesic (pain reliever) combined with Antihistamine (sleep aid)
purpose: This combination medication is used to help relieve minor aches and pains while also helping you fall asleep. It is commonly used for nighttime pain relief, such as headaches, muscle aches, or arthritis discomfort that keeps you awake. Think of it as a two-in-one: a pain reliever and a gentle sleep helper in one pill.
how_it_works: Acetaminophen works by blocking pain signals in your brain so you feel less discomfort. Diphenhydramine is an antihistamine that makes you feel drowsy by blocking a chemical in your brain called histamine, which normally keeps you alert. Together, they help ease your pain and make it easier for you to drift off to sleep.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include drowsiness, dry mouth, dizziness, and blurry vision. You may also feel groggy or have trouble waking up the next morning. Some people notice constipation or difficulty urinating as well.
warnings: Do not take this with alcohol, as combining alcohol with acetaminophen can seriously harm your liver. Do not use more than the recommended dose, and avoid other products that contain acetaminophen at the same time — too much acetaminophen can cause serious liver damage. This medication is for short-term use only — do not take it for more than 2 weeks without talking to your doctor. It is not recommended for people over age 65, those with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, or breathing problems. Do not drive or operate heavy machinery after taking this medication, as it causes significant drowsiness.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 2 tablets (each containing 500 mg acetaminophen and 25 mg diphenhydramine) taken by mouth at bedtime. Do not take more than 2 tablets in a 24-hour period. Only take it when you are ready to sleep for a full 7-8 hours. Do not give this to children under 12 without a doctor's advice.
